title: Residual Shares on Money Freed From a Claim Hold
content:
Where money is freed from a claim hold on a Keyturn Host Payout Account, part of what is answered is kept back against exposure that has not yet cooled. The residual share turns on how the account settles and on how long the claim hold has stood.

**Where the account settles only when the host asks and the claim hold has stood for longer than a calendar quarter**, being longer than 92 calendar days, the matured residual share of 0 percent applies.

**Where the account settles only when the host asks and the claim hold has stood for a calendar quarter or less**, being 92 calendar days or fewer, the fresh residual share of 10 percent applies.

**In every other case**, the standard residual share of 25 percent applies.

The share is taken on what the settlement money answers, and the part kept back is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

## The boundary, from both sides

The age of the claim hold is counted in calendar days from the day of the most recent reserve taken against an open claim on the account, up to the day the release is worked out. On an account that settles only when the host asks, a hold aged 92 days falls in the second case at 10 percent, a hold aged 93 days falls in the first at 0 percent, and a hold aged 91 days falls in the second likewise.

## Where the account settles on another rhythm

Both of the first two cases require that the account settles only when the host asks. An account swept on any other rhythm falls to the third case whatever the age of its claim hold, and the standard residual share of 25 percent applies to it.

## On hypothetical figures

Where what the settlement money answers is 2000.00 USD: nothing is kept back on an account that settles only when the host asks whose claim hold has stood 200 days; 200.00 USD is kept back where that same account's claim hold has stood 40 days; and 500.00 USD is kept back on an account swept on any other rhythm.
